name: Qatar International Islamic Bank
founded: 1990 (incorporated under Amiri Decree No. 52 of 1990; operations began 1 Jan 1991)
ownership_summary: QSE-listed. The H1 2026 investor presentation says the Qatar Investment Authority is the largest shareholder at 16%, held through Qatar Holding. Qatari companies and individuals own 63%, and GCC and foreign nationals 21%. The board is made up mainly of representatives of Qatari corporate shareholders, for example Medicare Group (Chairman) and Bright Side for Trading (Vice Chairman).
government_link: Yes - QIA holds 16% through Qatar Holding and is the largest shareholder (H1 2026 investor presentation).
group_structure: Qatar International Islamic Bank (Q.P.S.C.) is the listed operating bank. Its consolidated subsidiaries are sukuk-issuing vehicles only: QIIB Senior Oryx Ltd (QFC), QIIB Tier 1 Sukuk LLC and QIIB Tier 1 Sukuk Ltd. Associates at 31 Dec 2025: Umnia Bank, Morocco (40%, banking), Al Tashelat Islamic Company (49%, real estate), Contractor Co. (49%, contracting) and Mackeen Holding (49%, real estate, fully impaired). In Jul 2026 QIIB made a strategic investment in fintech SkipCash; the stake was not disclosed. There is no brokerage or asset management subsidiary.

QIIB Tier 1 Sukuk LLC / QIIB Tier 1 Sukuk Ltd

subsidiaries.activity: Real estate (Qatar); carrying value nil after impairment

footprint: Qatar only, apart from the 40% Moroccan associate Umnia Bank. The H1 2026 presentation gives 17 branches, 1 digital branch (Digital Lounge, Msheireb) and 75 ATMs. The FY2025 statements say head office plus 16 local branches. The presentation's segment page says 14 personal banking branches and 3 corporate branches.
customer_segments: Personal banking (mass retail; Joud prize savings account), QIIB Wajaha (affluent/premium package), QIIB Private Banking (HNW, by invitation), corporate, government and semi-government, and SMEs.
business_lines: Three segments: Personal Banking (financing, deposits, cards, Wajaha and Private Banking tiers); Corporate Banking (Murabahah, Ijarah, Mudarabah, Istisna, trade and project finance; government and SME); and Treasury & Investments (funding, the sukuk book and the bank's own investment and real estate portfolio). Treasury & Investments also offers customers 'Shariaa compliant complex investment opportunities': equity participation, private equity, investment funds and sukuk. It is also a joint lead manager on Qatari sukuk issues.

capabilities.wealth_summary: QIIB's wealth offer is limited and banking-led. Personal Banking, run by Chief of Personal Banking Zakaria Glaoui, has two premium tiers. QIIB Wajaha is the affluent package (QR 50,000 monthly salary or QR 1m balance). QIIB Private Banking is by invitation only and offers a dedicated 24/7 RM, Mastercard World Elite and lifestyle privileges; its pages describe no investment products. Investment opportunities for customers come from the Treasury & Investments department under Sheikh Mohammed Bin Ali Al Thani: equity participation, private equity, investment funds and sukuk, all Shari'a-compliant. No asset manager, brokerage subsidiary, AUM or in-app investing was found. The QIIB Mobile app covers payments, transfers, cards and a rewards shop. On 30 Jul 2026 QIIB signed an MoU with The Group Securities, a Qatari broker, to provide 'reciprocal services and advanced digital tools' for capital-market investors and 'a seamless and integrated investment and banking experience'. QIIB's 2025-2026 digital activity has centred on payments: the SkipCash strategic investment (Jul 2026), a Visa alliance, the AFAQ payments system and the QIIB Online Shop.

segments.name: QIIB Wajaha
segments.eligibility: Free membership with a monthly salary of QR 50,000 or more, or a minimum balance of QR 1,000,000 or more.

private_banking.detail: QIIB Private: invitation-only HNW service with a dedicated 24/7 RM, Mastercard World Elite, a loyalty programme, a dedicated call centre, valet parking and lifestyle benefits. No investment products are described on the page.

asset_management.detail: No asset management subsidiary or proprietary fund range. The group's subsidiaries are sukuk SPVs only (S3). Treasury & Investments manages the bank's own portfolio and offers customers investment funds, but no manager or fund names are given.

brokerage.detail: No in-house brokerage. MoU of 30 Jul 2026 with The Group Securities (Qatari broker; relationship of 'more than thirty years') for reciprocal services and digital tools for capital-market investors. Implementation status unknown.

digital_investing.detail: The QIIB Mobile features listed (transfers, Western Union, QMP eWallet, card controls, bill payments, rewards shop) include no investing. IPO subscriptions are taken through QIIB channels, for example the Dandy IPO (home page banner). The Group Securities MoU aims at 'a seamless and integrated investment and banking experience'.

advisory.detail: The Treasury & Investment team offers customers 'the highest possible standards of guidance' on Shari'a-compliant local, regional and international investments. There is no formal advisory proposition or wealth RM investment service.

funds_platform.detail: 'Investment funds' are listed among Treasury & Investment services for customers, with no fund names or platform.

private_markets.detail: 'Equity participation' and 'private equity' are listed among Treasury & Investment services offered to customers, with no products named.

islamic_wealth.detail: Fully Shari'a-compliant bank. Customers can access sukuk, investment funds and equity and private-equity participation through Treasury & Investments.

QIIB became a strategic investor in the QFC-licensed payments fintech
'Strategic Alliance: QIIB and Visa Join Forces to Advance Innovation in Payment Solutions' (heading only; release ID 566 sits between releases dated 5 and 20 Jul 2026)

initiatives.what: MoU with The Group Securities for an integrated investment and banking experience.
Launched the QIIB Online Shop rewards marketplace with instant redemption through mobile banking.
Joined the AFAQ GCC payments system. Won MEA Finance 'Best Innovation in Retail Banking, Qatar 2026'.

opportunities: No investing in the QIIB Mobile app and no in-house brokerage or asset manager. The Jul 2026 MoU with The Group Securities explicitly targets 'a seamless and integrated investment and banking experience' (S13, S19).
Invitation-only Private Banking and the Wajaha affluent tier are built on lifestyle benefits; no investment proposition is described (S9, S11).
Treasury & Investments already offers customers funds, sukuk and private equity, but with no platform, named products or digital channel (S10).
Management stresses digital transformation and fintech partnerships, such as the SkipCash investment and the Visa alliance (S4, S20).
barriers: Fully Islamic: needs Shari'a-screened products approved by its Shari'a Supervisory Board (S3).
Recent digital investment has gone to payments rather than wealth, and brokerage integration is going through The Group Securities (S13, S20).
Small premium segment, no published AUM, and no named wealth head below the Chief of Personal Banking (S7, S9).

Mastercard - World Elite card for Private Banking (S9)

discrepancies.detail: The QIIB release of 21 Mar 2018 (S27) says he joined QIIB in 2009 (Treasury and Investment Department); the Governance Reports (S23) give 2016 as the start date.
discrepancies.resolution: Both recorded; his appointment as Chief on 21 Mar 2018 is not affected.

open_items: Q3 2026 (30 Sep 2026) results not yet on QSE: the API returned 404 for QIIK 2026-09-30 on 12 Oct 2026.

The Executive Management page gives names and titles only. Biographies came from the Governance Report 2025 (Arabic; education only for the CEO and Deputy CEO; joining years for all executives) and from QIIB releases. Education and earlier careers of the Chief of Personal Banking, CIO, COO, CFO, CRO and HR chief are not published in any source opened.

Yousef el-Maraghi (Head of Private Banking and Wealth Management) appears only in the 8 Jul 2026 release (S28): no bio, appointment date or LinkedIn profile found. No named head of Wajaha or of digital/alternative channels was found. Khalid Abdulrahman Al-Shaibei is 'Chief Business Development Officer' (Nov 2023, Feb 2026) or 'Head of Business Development Sector' (Jun 2026) in releases, a sector that previously covered alternative channels (S16), but he is not on the Executive Management page or in the Governance Report 2025 list; not added.

The Executive Management page now lists a Chief of Compliance & Anti Financial Crimes (Mohammad Ahmad Rifaie; the Governance Report 2025 also lists the Head of the Audit Sector) who is not in this file (not a decision-maker function). Other heads quoted in 2025-2026 releases and not profiled: Talal al-Jaidah (Head of Banking Products), Abdulla Hamad al-Mesaifri (Head of Branch Network), Najeeb Ahmed Nasiruddin (Head of Payments & International Operations), Mahmoud Ahmed Al-Ahmad (Head of Treasury and Investment, Jan 2024).

Not profiled in this file: nine other board members of the 2026-2028 board (S24) and the three members of the Shariah Supervisory Board, renewed for three years at the 26 Mar 2026 AGM (Sheikh Dr. Walid Bin Hadi, Chairman; Sheikh Abdoulaziz KH H A AlQassar; Sheikh Dr. Mohammed Ohmain; official page https://www.qiib.com.qa/Page/Details/99). Add them if board or Shariah contacts are needed.

Chairman check: the H1 2026 results release (20 Jul 2026) was announced by the Vice Chairman and Managing Director, who also chaired the approving board meeting (S4), while the FY2025 and Q1 2026 releases were announced by the Chairman (S36, S35). No change of Chairman is published and the official Board page lists him; re-check on the Q3 2026 release.

LinkedIn: role-based searches on 2026-10-13 matched only the CIO (S34). No profile found for CEO Al Shaibei, Chief of Personal Banking Glaoui, Chief of Treasury and Investment Sheikh Mohammed or the private banking head. A company page 'QIIBOFFICIAL' (linkedin.com/company/qiib-qatar) appeared in search results but is not linked from qiib.com.qa, so linkedin_company stays null (outside this pass).

The AGM minutes of 26 Mar 2026 (https://www.qiib.com.qa/Documents/Download/392) are a scanned PDF with no extractable text; the AGM release (S24) was used instead. The World Policy Conference profile (S18) could not be opened on 2026-10-13 (connection reset).
The scope and launch timing of The Group Securities MoU (30 Jul 2026) are not published. Check whether in-app trading follows.
Treasury & Investment customer products (funds, private equity) have no named products or providers.
No customer, employee or AUM figures are published in the 2025 annual report or the H1 2026 presentation.
